detail: p. 2217: Transplacental digoxin is an option with uncertain benefit in fetal heart failure.

p. 2218: The selection description requires demonstrable antegrade valvar flow, minimal or absent subvalvar obstruction and evidence of evolution toward HLHS.
p. 2218: The cited cohort had 52 technical successes among 70 procedures (74%).
p. 2218: The counselling paragraphs address procedural risks, alternative management and unknown long-term outcomes.
p. 2218: Specialist congenital cardiac care at and after delivery is recommended in this setting.

p. 2218: The extreme mortality and critical presentation are attributed specifically to a highly restrictive or intact atrial septum. The same page describes lesser degrees of restriction as typical in HLHS.
p. 2218: The two Doppler assessments support grading atrial obstruction. The diminished oxygen response is an indirect sign.
p. 2218: Technique selection and the timing needed to limit pulmonary vascular damage are explicitly unresolved.
p. 2218–2219: In the described syndrome, dilated left-sided structures can compress the right heart. Hydrops, when present, is usually fatal.
p. 2219: The discussion limits consideration to selected PA/IVS cases and describes possible fetal survival benefit with severe TR and hydrops when demise is anticipated.
p. 2219: Adequate tricuspid size can permit staged postnatal rehabilitation despite a very small RV.
p. 2219: Both ranges match the 2014 statement and the mortality estimate explicitly concerns untreated TTTS.
p. 2219: Recipient cardiac abnormalities and persistence of some RV outflow lesions after successful laser therapy are supported.
p. 2219: The text explains the omission in Quintero staging and the alternative cardiac scores. Tables 17 and 18 appear on the following page.
p. 2220: Echocardiography is recommended during TTTS diagnosis and initial management.
p. 2219–2220: The text describes limited and conflicting evidence for outcome prediction using cardiovascular findings.
p. 2220: Surviving twins should be considered for echocardiography at 24–48 hours after the procedure.

p. 2222: Available studies did not demonstrate an inherent advantage. An unqualified statement that none exists is stronger. The absence of randomised trials was reported in 2014 for severe CHD.

p. 2226: The wording distinguishes indicated conversion or rhythm control for uncontrolled tachycardia from reasonable chronotropic support or pacing in CHB.

p. 2223: Table 19 level 5 specifies listing after 35 weeks, caesarean when a heart is available and a specialist team.
